sections.h2: How is Louisiana divided, and who handles what for a house sale?
sections.html:
Louisiana has 64 parishes where other states have counties. It is one of only three states that avoid the word county for its main subdivisions, along with Alaska and Connecticut. For a seller, the parish is the unit that matters, because the offices that touch a house sale are organized around it.

Governance differs from one parish to the next. Thirty-eight parishes are run by a police jury, while the other 26 use a council-president, council-manager, parish commission or consolidated city and parish model. New Orleans is a consolidated city-parish.

FactFigure
Parishes in the state64
Most peopleEast Baton Rouge Parish, 456,180
Fewest peopleTensas Parish, 3,700
Largest by areaPlaquemines Parish, 2,429 square miles
Smallest by areaWest Baton Rouge Parish, 203 square miles
Parishes run by a police jury38

Before you plan a closing date, call the parish assessor, the clerk of court and the sheriff for the parish where the house sits. Our page on Louisiana guides by city and county points to the parish pages we have built so far.

sections.h2: What does an as-is cash sale mean under Louisiana law?
sections.html:
An as-is sale means the buyer takes the house in its present condition and the seller agrees to limit or exclude the usual warranty against hidden defects. Louisiana Civil Code Article 2548 allows that. The wording has to be clear and unambiguous and brought to the buyer's attention.

A buyer is not bound by an exclusion when the seller declared that the house had a quality the seller knew it did not have.

A transfer of real estate also needs the right form. Civil Code Article 1839 says a transfer of immovable property must be made by authentic act or by act under private signature. Ask who is handling title and what that office charges before you sign a purchase agreement.

Settle these in writing with any cash buyer:

  • Who pays for the title search, the notary and the recording
  • Whether the as-is clause appears in the purchase agreement and the act of sale
  • What happens to any deposit if the buyer cancels, and who clears out what is left in the house

sections.h2: What must a Louisiana seller disclose?
sections.html:
A seller of residential property must complete a property disclosure document on a form from the Louisiana Real Estate Commission, or a form with at least its minimum language. R.S. 9:3198 covers the rules.

The seller completes it in good faith, to the best of the seller's knowledge. If the seller does not know something, the form can say so. The completed form goes to the buyer no later than the moment the buyer makes an offer. If it arrives after an offer, the buyer can walk away without penalty within 72 hours, not counting weekends and holidays, and the deposit comes back.

The form has Louisiana-specific questions. It asks whether the buyer must join a homeowners' association, whether restrictive covenants or building restrictions apply, and whether an illegal methamphetamine lab was ever on the property. It also asks whether a cavity made by dissolving a salt stock with water sits under the property, and whether the house is within 2,640 feet of a solution mining injection well.

The disclosure is not a warranty and does not replace an inspection. A seller is not liable for an error that was not a willful misrepresentation. Starting January 1, 2027, the duty also reaches vacant residential property.

The statute does not name flood history or foundation problems, so read the current commission form for those lines. If you are unsure how to answer, ask a Louisiana attorney.

sections.h2: Who records the deed, and what does recording cost?
sections.html:
The clerk of court in each parish also acts as the recorder of documents. R.S. 13:844 says clerks of the district courts, as ex officio recorders, charge set fees for filing and recording. The fee depends on page count.

Document lengthRecording fee
1 to 5 pages$100
6 to 25 pages$200
26 to 50 pages$300
Over 50 pages$300 for the first 50, plus $5 per added page

The fees include indexing up to ten names and one certified copy. Ask the office for its current fee list. We have written clerk guides for Orleans, Jefferson, Lafayette, Terrebonne, Ouachita, Livingston and Washington parishes.

We did not find a statewide transfer tax on deeds in the sources we reviewed. Ask the clerk of court and your closing office what applies in your parish. If you plan to use a quitclaim, read our page on the Louisiana quitclaim deed first.

sections.h2: How does foreclosure work in Louisiana?
sections.html:
Louisiana lenders often use executory proceedings. Under Code of Civil Procedure Article 2631, these proceedings seize and sell property without previous citation and judgment, to enforce a mortgage or privilege shown by an authentic act that imports a confession of judgment.

The steps that follow are set out in the code:

  • The sheriff seizes the property as soon as the writ of seizure and sale arrives (Article 2721).
  • The sheriff serves the owner with a written notice of seizure, which for a residence must include housing counseling information. If the sale is an online auction, the notice gives the date, opening time and web address.
  • The sheriff advertises the sale (Article 2722).
  • The property must be appraised before the sale unless the mortgage document waived appraisal and the court order allows a sale without it (Article 2723).

We did not confirm a standard number of days from a missed payment to the sale. If you received a notice of seizure, you still have options, including selling before the sheriff's sale. Confirm the sale date with the sheriff's office named on the notice and speak with a Louisiana attorney or housing counselor.

sections.h2: What happens to an inherited house in Louisiana?
sections.html:
Louisiana calls probate a succession, and a small succession is the shorter route. Under Code of Civil Procedure Article 3421, a person who died domiciled in Louisiana qualifies if the property's gross value at date of death was $200,000 or less.

SituationSmall succession limit
Died domiciled in Louisiana$200,000 gross value
Died domiciled elsewhere, with Louisiana property$125,000 gross value
Death at least 20 years before the affidavitAny value

The legislature amended the article as recently as 2026, so confirm the figure with the clerk of court before you rely on it. A larger estate needs a fuller court process before the heirs can sign a deed. See our guides to the Louisiana probate process and to estate and inheritance tax.

If a succession is still open, tell the buyer early so the title work can be planned around it.

sections.h2: How does the homestead exemption affect a seller?
sections.html:
The Louisiana Constitution, Article VII, Section 20, exempts a bona fide homestead from state, parish and special ad valorem taxes on the first $7,500 of assessed valuation. The homestead can cover up to 160 acres with buildings, and the owner has to occupy it.

The exemption lowers the tax bill and does not erase it. Taxes on the house still need to be settled at closing. See our pages on the homestead exemption and the Louisiana property tax guide. If your parish has its own guide, such as Orleans, Jefferson or Caddo, use it to find the assessor's contact details.

sections.h2: What if the house has a tenant?
sections.html:
A sale does not cancel a lease. Under Civil Code Article 2711, a transfer of the leased thing by the lessor does not end the lease, and the tenant can sue the lessor for loss caused by the transfer. A buyer should expect to take a tenant along with the building unless the tenant leaves first.

When an owner does want possession, Code of Civil Procedure Article 4701 requires written notice to vacate. The notice gives the tenant not less than five days from delivery. For a lease with a definite term, notice can go out no more than 30 days before the term ends. A tenant can waive the notice in the lease.

Security deposits also follow the house. R.S. 9:3251 says a residential deposit is returned within one month after the lease ends, minus amounts reasonably needed for a default or unreasonable wear. Owners selling a rental should pull the lease, gather the deposit records and tell the buyer in writing who lives in the house.

Read our pages on landlord and tenant law, the eviction notice rules and the eviction process for more detail. If someone is living in the house without a lease, see squatters rights and adverse possession.

sections.h2: Where should I start in my own parish?
sections.html: Start with the parish name on your tax bill, then use the list below. Where a parish shows only a clerk or tax guide, we have no city page there yet, so the parish office is the best first call.

faqs.q: How many parishes does Louisiana have?
faqs.a: Sixty-four. Thirty-eight are run by a police jury and the rest use other forms of government.

faqs.q: Do I have to repair the house before an as-is sale?
faqs.a: No law requires it. Civil Code Article 2548 lets you limit the warranty against hidden defects if the wording is clear and brought to the buyer's attention.

faqs.q: When does the buyer get the disclosure form?
faqs.a: No later than the offer. If it arrives after, the buyer can cancel without penalty within 72 hours, not counting weekends and holidays.

faqs.q: What does recording a deed cost?
faqs.a: Under R.S. 13:844, $100 for one to five pages, $200 for six to 25 pages and $300 for 26 to 50 pages.
Often yes, before the sheriff's sale. Check the date on your notice and speak with an attorney.

faqs.q: Can I sell an inherited house without full probate?
faqs.a: If the estate is a small succession, the process is shorter. The limit is $200,000 for a Louisiana resident. Confirm it with the clerk.

faqs.q: Does a tenant have to leave when I sell?
faqs.a: No. Under Civil Code Article 2711, a transfer of the house does not end the lease.
